old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-p4mf","title":"announce_store accept(): failed floor write leaves stale cache entry that can regress the durable state","description":"Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-t8ox. rust/lichen-node/src/announce_store.rs:394-403: on the durable path, write(iid,false,next) commits the new state record, then write(iid,true,next)? at line 401 early-returns Err(Io) on failure, skipping remember(iid,next) at line 403. For an existing pin, load(iid) at line 378 cached the OLD state, so after the failed accept: cache=old, durable state=new, durable floor=old. Every subsequent load() takes the cache fast path (308-311) and returns the old state despite the durable record holding the new one, and a subsequent accept() validates against the stale cached state, so a replayed/held announce with old.seq \u003c seq \u003c new.seq (RFC 1982) passes the seq_gt check at 383 and is written over the newer durable state record - the sealed state regresses and an already-seen announce is re-accepted. The header's state-then-floor crash analysis (lines 10-13) assumes a crash destroys the cache; a non-fatal floor-write error (ENOSPC/EIO on the floor root) violates that while the cache survives. Fix: on the floor-write error path, self.records.remove(iid) before returning Err so the next load() rebuilds from disk (state=new, floor=old lag heals forward to new). Removal is the fail-safe option; caching next also works since durable state is next, but removal is simpler.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-08-30T20:22:17.591633901Z","created_by":"opencode-worker-2","updated_at":"2026-08-30T20:22:17.591633901Z","dependencies":[{"issue_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-p4mf","depends_on_id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-t8ox","type":"discovered-from","created_at":"2026-08-30T20:22:17.73462039Z","created_by":"opencode-worker-2","metadata":"{}"}]}
